text:
julie: Heads-up — running into a weird typing regression when using the JS SDK in Edge ESM builds. Generic overloads that accept <T> end up inferred as `any` (or error) in our Cloudflare Worker bundle. Seems related to tsconfig + module resolution + how the package ships .d.ts.

sam: Can you paste a tiny repro? stack or example signature helps.

julie: Yep. Minimal example:

julie: ```ts
// sdk/index.d.ts (simplified)
export function call<T>(opts: { input: T }): Promise<Result<T>>;
export function call(opts: { input: unknown }): Promise<Result<any>>;
```

julie: When imported in an edge app: `client.call({ input: { foo: 1 } })` TS infers the param as `any` and gives no autocomplete. Locally (node target) inference is fine.

tyler: That pattern (overload + unknown fallback) is fragile across module modes. TS chooses the first overload that matches and ESM consumers sometimes pick the wrong entry because of how types are resolved (package exports / typesVersions).

maria: Are you bundling with esbuild/webpack/swc? Some bundlers rewrite imports and strip `types` mapping, so the consumer ends up resolving .d.ts from a different path (CJS vs ESM). Cloudflare builds often squash to ESM and change resolution.

julie: Using Wrangler + esbuild. tsconfig: module=es2020, moduleResolution=node, target=es2020. package.json has both "module" and "main" and a top-level "types" pointing to dist/index.d.ts.

omar: Two quick things to try: 1) publish types with a clear ESM mapping via "exports"/"types": {"import": "dist/esm/index.d.ts", "require": "dist/cjs/index.d.ts"} or use typesVersions in package.json. 2) make the overloads less ambiguous: prefer a single generic with conditional constraint instead of two overloads.

omar: Example rewrite: 

omar: ```ts
export function call<T = unknown>(opts: { input: T & {} }): Promise<Result<T>>;
// or use conditional: type InputOf<T> = unknown extends T ? any : T;
```

sam: Also try toggling "skipLibCheck": true temporarily to see if a downstream lib type is interfering. But that's a bandaid.

maria: For edge-specific TS tooling, set target/es2022 and lib ["es2022","dom"] so inference for ESM runtime features is consistent. Also module=esnext + moduleResolution=node16/node20 can help with package exports resolution.

julie: Good tips. One puzzling detail: tsc --declaration on CI produces a different .d.ts than local build, even with the same tsc version. Could packaging scripts be rewriting types?

tyler: That can happen if rollup/tsup emits types from source vs compiled output. Ensure CI runs `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` from the same tsconfig you publish. If you use build step that copies types, double-check paths.

maria: Another workaround: export a thin, non-overloaded wrapper in the public surface that delegates to the complex implementation. Wrappers preserve inference better for consumers: `export function create<T>(opts: T) { return internalCreate(opts as any); }` not ideal but reduces TS overload resolution weirdness.

julie: Would adding an explicit "typesVersions" map for modern TS consumers be a blocker for older ones?

omar: You can target TS >=4.7 for node16/node20 resolution, and provide a fallback for older compilers. typesVersions lets you specify which d.ts to pick for which TS versions.

julie: I'll try: 1) reproduce minimal repo, 2) publish a temp package with explicit exports/types mappings, 3) attempt the generic refactor. I'll drop a sample repo link when ready. :pray:

dev-bot: build-triggered: julie pushed branch ts-edge-typing-fix — CI started (checklink).

sam: If you want, I can help make the tiny repro and a test matrix (node/bun/cloudflare) so we can capture where inference breaks.

julie: Yes please — assign me and sam to a small issue. Also adding this to the devex sample-app checklist so new hires hit this case.

tyler: Quick pro-tip: inline JSDoc generic hints for consumers sometimes help editors without changing types: `/** @template T */` on exported funcs. Not a long-term fix but lowers friction for onboarding.

julie: Action items: create repro repo, try typesExports/typesVersions, attempt single-generic refactor, add sample-app test. I'll post the link here. Thanks all :thumbsup:
